title: Safety corridor auto-calibrator for canary exits (cost + latency aware)
creator: Maya Chen
description: Problem: Current canary rollout safeguards use fixed thresholds or simple percentile guards which either (a) trigger noisy false positives during diurnal traffic swings or (b) miss subtle token-cost regressions. We need an automated calibration component that composes multiple SLO signals (latency, 95/99p tail, error rate, token cost per request, and throughput) into a stable 'safety corridor' and adjusts canary exit thresholds per-route/cohort.
goals: 1) Produce per-route and per-cohort dynamic exit bands (upper/lower) that adapt to baseline shifts and traffic volume. 2) Make rollback decisioning cost-aware so token-price regressions can trigger protective action alongside latency/errors. 3) Provide explainable signal fusion (weighting and z-score normalization) for on-call and audit. 4) Add a small offline calibration harness to recommend conservative defaults before enabling auto-eviction.
acceptance_criteria:
- System computes an adaptive upper/lower bound for each SLO signal per route and cohort in real-time.
- Canary with injected 2x token-cost increase on a synthetic cohort is automatically pulled or reduced to 0% traffic within configured cooldown.
- False positive rate (rollbacks during stable periods) is <0.5% on a 30d holdout traffic slice.
- System exposes a UI view that lists contributing signals, their normalized scores, and the composite decision score for any active canary.
- Offline calibration tool outputs suggested multiplier defaults and confidence intervals for at least 90% of active routes when run on 14d historical data.
design_notes:
- Normalization: use rolling-window robust z-scores (median + MAD) per-signal and per-cohort to reduce sensitivity to outliers and diurnal patterns.
- Fusion: compute a weighted harmonic aggregation for cost/throughput sensitive signals and an inverse-variance weighted mean for latency/error signals; final composite = sigmoid(linear combination) to map into 0..1 risk score.
- Thresholding: map composite risk to action bands: advisory (risk>0.45), throttled diversion (risk>0.65), emergency retreat (risk>0.85). These cutpoints are initially conservative and tunable.
- Calibration: offline module runs Bayesian credible-interval estimation on 14/30d windows and suggests per-route multipliers to achieve target false-positive budgets.
- Cohorts: baseline per-customer and per-region cohorts; fall back to global route baseline when cohort data insufficient.
- Cost signal: compute token-cost per request delta normalized by historical variance and weighted by revenue-significance label (high/low).
implementation_notes:
- Runtime service: new 'safety-corridor' microservice that subscribes to existing metrics stream (Prometheus/cortex or telemetry bus) and publishes per-route canary advisories over the control plane.
- Integrations: hook into rollout controller to accept advisory scores and implement actions (divert, throttle, rollback).
- Config: per-team policy YAML with weights, cool-downs, and action mappings; console UI will expose safe defaults and 'enable auto-evict' toggle.
- Backwards compat: if disabled, controller uses existing static thresholds.
- Observability: emit debug traces of the fusion computation and persisted historical composites for audit.
test_plan:
- Unit tests for normalization and aggregation math (edge cases: low-sample cohorts).
- End-to-end test: simulated traffic harness that replays 30d of production and injects faults (latency spike, 1% error burst, token-cost jump) to validate expected action bands.
- Canary experiment: roll to 5 internal services with auto-evict disabled then enable in advisory mode, collect metrics for 2 weeks, then enable throttle and finally emergency retreat on one service as controlled test.
- Load: ensure safety-corridor service handles metric fanout for 10k active routes without tail latency > 200ms.
rollout_plan:
1) Alpha: run offline calibration on top-200 routes and present recommendations to SRE/PM. (2 weeks)
2) Beta: enable advisory-only mode for top-50 production canaries; monitor explainability UI and false-positive signal. (2 weeks)
3) Pilot: enable throttle actions for partner customers with SLO guardrails; require manual confirmation for emergency retreat. (3 weeks)
4) Gradual enable: flip auto-evict on for low-risk routes after 6-week observation, progressively widen to full fleet.
- Each stage has abort criteria: >1% unexpected rollbacks, >10% traffic instability on pilot customers, or stale calibration warnings.
open_questions:
- What default weightings should product set for cost vs latency for public tenants? (propose initial: cost 0.25, latency 0.5, error 0.25)
- How should revenue-significance labels be surfaced and maintained? Git-driven mapping or UI?
- Can we reuse existing metric ingest infra or do we need a sidecar sensor for per-request token-cost?
